In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the right PPC is a key region for visuospatial perception and that left PPC is also involved in the same process, although in a less specific manner.
the hot spot is not a fixed anatomical point, but it is located within a 3 cm x 3 cm area of the right PPC.
the hot spot for the modulation of visuospratial perception during line bisiestion judgment is in the right pariteal cortex, in the posterior part of the right pariteo-occipital sulcus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TMS can be used as a functional tool for mapping the neural substrates of visuospatial attention, and that this technique may also have potential therapeutic applications in patients with visuospatial neglect.
the optimal parietotemporal site for TMS to modulate visuospaial perception can be identified using the hunting protocol we propose.
the optimal site for TMS to induce left neglect-like bias in healthy subjects is the most anterior and dorsal portion of right parietal cortex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal stimulation site is not a fixed point but rather a region of the right parieto-occipital sulcus, whose size depends on the task used.

the optimal site of stimulation for modulating visuospatial perception in healthy participants can be identified using single-pulse stimulation, and that the optimal site is not the same for left PPC and right PPC.
the optimal site for modulating visuospatial perception with TMS is located in a relatively wide area of the right parieto-occipital junction and in the left parietal cortex.
